newsitem.title: USA: US junk bond funds reverse outflow trend-AMG Data.
newsitem.headline: US junk bond funds reverse outflow trend-AMG Data.

text.p: U.S. high-yield mutual funds received net cash inflows of $101 million in the week ended April 16, reversing a five-week trend of net cash outflows, according to AMG Data Services.
The last time high-yield mutual funds registered net cash inflows was the week ended March 12, 1997, with a total of $171 million.
The number represents high-yield mutual funds that report on a weekly basis.

"The (high-yield) market was doing much better this week," said Sam DeRosa-Farag, director of high-yield strategy at Chase Securities Inc. "If one believes there is a correlation between performance and cash flows, this upturn shouldn't be a surprise."
The recent inflows are also consistent with the widely-held view that most of the recent junk-bond mutual fund redemptions came from market timers, DeRose-Farag said.
Market timers are professional money managers who are known for moving large amounts of money into and out of the market, often on a short-term basis.
Becuase market timers make investment decisions based on price momentum, he noted that much of the same money that has left the market may now come back if junk bond prices continue to rise.
But DeRosa-Farag said that retail investors, in general, are continuing to hold back from investing in the capital markets.
He said he based this view on the recent trend of redemptions in equity mutual funds, which are less influenced by professional money managers than high-yield mutual funds.
Over the past five weeks, the four-week moving average of fund flows in all equity funds has dropped to 0.12 percent from 0.27 percent, according to AMG.
AMG, based in Arcata, Calif., is a U.S. mutual fund information company.
